Frontposten 3 is a ring of fires. Hounds in the courtyard,
brass on the walls, and in the middle of it Mori with a
Neuling! Die Eiserne! Gods, it's good to see ugly faces.
Clear my yard and we'll talk!

The pot's broken. I'll write that on my wall, if I
still have one in the morning.
The Marshal's bird got here. A cauldron, he says. I've

The breach is stone now, and the stone has a sally
port. Through the inner gate, through the keep, and I'll

Six years I held that gap from this side.

parameters: desc = Through the inner gate of Frontposten 3 and out of the sally port onto the Aschenfeld. The cauldron is in the Host's camp.
The inner gate. Mori's people hold it shut.
The inner gate, and beyond the keep the new stone of the
breach with its little iron sally port.
The inner gate. The ash can wait.
Frontposten 3, after. The Host has gone back into the ash
as if a tide went out. Mori's soldiers sleep where they
fell down. Nobody has gotten up again wearing brass.
The woman from the ash sits at the brazier with you and
Tsukishiro Yukino. The Frost Saint. S-rank, once. She
hasn't said a word in twelve years. Kills more of them
than a company, though, when she comes.
She walks out of the Aschenfeld every few months, sleeps
a night by a Wall fire and walks back in. Nobody asks.
You came for us. Out there. Why?
Kagerō. When he watched your light cut the chain. From
the other side of the ash. I felt it.
The Demon Lord has a name?
He had a mother, and a sword, and four friends. We were
five. The Morgenwacht. The Guild's best, twelve years
ago. We went into the rift at Frostheim to close it.
Something in the miasma spoke to him. Hōkai, I think.
It told him everything could stop. War. Heroes. Being
needed, being sent, being the one who dies next.
He listened. The others died. I came back. The rift kept
He spares children because he still remembers being one.
He kills heroes because he still remembers being one.
And inside the miasma nothing touches him. Swords go
through him like smoke. The Veil of Ash.
I knew the last one. In the year 312 the first Demon Lord
wore the same veil, and Sōryū Akira cut it open with
You knew the hero of the Dawn War.
I was one of her generals, my Lord. Later. Not tonight.
I don't come out of that story well.
The Morgenklinge. The Sternlaterne. The Heldenhorn. The
Aschenkrone. Each one pierces one step of a demon's rank.
All four, and the veil tears.
…If I say his name to him, he might remember. Once.
I will come with you. If you'll let me.
You won't be. I don't talk.
Neither do I. We'll get on.
Morning. A rider from the Wallfeste with the princess's
colours, and a letter under the seal of Asahina.
(in the letter) Kanta. The Wall stands. The Marshal is
asleep on his feet and the Host is back in the ash.
(in the letter) Hanma's regalia are in the court records:
the Morgenklinge went to the Emperor in 313 and it is
still in the vault at Lichtenhall. The Empress won't
(in the letter) give it to a vessel from the Wall because
a princess asks. So take this letter and ask her anyway.
She's holding her Sonnwende tournament. Be persuasive.
\C[6]Yukino\C[0], the Frost Saint, joins the party.
